interpretation: Some hold that there is an intermediate because they cannot answer eristic arguments, others because they seek an argument for everything (1012a17-21). Against all of them the starting point is definition, and definition arises from their having to signify something, since the account of which the name is a sign will be a definition (1012a21-24). Read as the IV.4 elenctic strategy applied to excluded middle: the defence starts from what the opponent grants by speaking significantly, not from a demonstration of the law. Methodological; not formalized as a Lean proposition. The formal results LOGIC-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE-IRREFUTABLE and LOGIC-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE-NOT-DENIABLE capture one part of the point (a denial of an instance refutes itself), not the appeal to signification.
